summary: The bill authorizes $15 billion per year for fiscal years 2026-2035 for the HOME, CDBG, and Housing Trust Fund programs but restricts those funds to high-cost areas, and requires HUD to assess and report on alternative area median income calculations and other metrics to increase affordable housing supply in urban areas.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $15 billion annually for 10 years ($5B each for HOME, CDBG, and Housing Trust Fund) targeted at high-cost housing areas. This is a direct, large-scale expansion of federal appropriations for housing programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue policy.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, or public health programs.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No provisions address immigration, visas, border policy, or immigrant eligibility.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions relate to military, defense, or national security spending.
No provisions address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy standards.

The bill substantially expands three major federal affordable housing programs (HOME, CDBG, Housing Trust Fund) with new multi-year appropriations. These are core safety-net housing assistance mechanisms, so the bill directly enlarges the social safety net.
No provisions address schools, school funding, or education policy.
No provisions address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-abuse programs.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
By authorizing $150 billion in new mandatory-style appropriations over a decade, the bill increases federal outlays and therefore contributes to deficit spending rather than debt reduction.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or nondiscrimination rules.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions address voting rights, election administration, or voter access.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or labor standards.
No provisions address religious exemptions or civil-rights enforcement.
